note: Every fixture is a project at some layout state. The skill must resolve the format before it writes anything, hand an old layout to stack-it:migrate rather than restructuring it, and keep generated stack content out of CLAUDE.md in every case. The agent-facing reference is two files. docs/stack.md is the tier every agent loads through the AGENTS.md pointer, so it stays small: what the project is, a Commands table with a row only for the tasks the project really has, a two-column Pins table, at most 15 Rules, and a plain-path pointer to the notes file. docs/stack-notes.md is the tier read on demand and carries the detail behind every pin. Each file is a header line, a generated section between <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> markers, and a tail below the end marker that belongs to the user; ownership is decided by the header's '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format N' prefix, since the sentence after it changed between versions, and a symlink at either path is never ours. Format 2 always writes a marker pair into both files, so an owned docs file with no markers is malformed for this layout and stops the run: the intermediate 0.5.x layouts (a docs/stack.md with no markers, a single-file reference) are unsupported and nothing migrates from them. The pointer from docs/stack.md to docs/stack-notes.md is a plain path and never an @ import, since an @ path would load the notes file at every session start. Carried notes only ever land in docs/stack-notes.md's tail. Fixtures with tails (proj-already-documented, proj-both-tails-carry) pin that both tails survive a regeneration. Fixtures for stop cases (foreign-stack-doc, format-ahead-of-plugin, malformed-stack-doc, malformed-notes-doc, no-markers-stack-doc, hand-written-notes, lockfile-format-3) hold only what triggers the stop, since the skill halts before it writes.

evals.name: from-lockfile
evals.prompt: I want my project's tech stack documented so both my coding agents and new contributors know what we're using and how to run things. Put the agent-facing reference where any agent will find it, and the human-facing part in the README. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The virgin case. Format resolves to 2 off the lockfile's format key, and there is no docs/stack.md, no docs/stack-notes.md, no pointer and no bridge, so this project has never been documented and migrate does not run. Documents from .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml, which validates, with versions matching it exactly, and writes BOTH tiers. docs/stack.md gets the header on line 1, '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives. Rationale, wiring, and carried notes live in docs/stack-notes.md.', a blank line, then exactly one <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> pair holding: one or two sentences saying what the project is and that the notes file holds the why; a Commands table; a Pins table of exactly TWO columns, tool and version, under group headings; and a Rules list, one line each, at most 15 and only the ones the lockfile and the code support. package.json defines exactly four scripts (dev, build, test, lint), so the Commands table has SIX rows: install, add a dependency, dev, build, test, lint. There is no format row and no run/start row, because this project has neither script; inventing one, or writing a row that says 'not configured', is a failure. The notes tier says which of the eight tasks have no command. The Rules carry only what an agent gets wrong unprompted (npm is the package manager, Tailwind v4 is wired through the Vite plugin so there is no tailwind.config.js, ESLint is flat config from eslint.config.js, Vite 7 needs Node 20.19+); padding the list toward 15 with guesses is a failure. No sentence about what a tool is for or how it is wired appears anywhere in docs/stack.md outside a Rules line: role and wiring are the notes tier's job. The LAST line inside the markers is the plain-path pointer 'Detail for every pin, the wiring, and the notes carried forward from earlier docs: docs/stack-notes.md. Read it before changing configuration or adding a tool.', with NO '@' before the path and no markdown link around it: an '@' there would make Claude Code load the notes file at every session start, which is the whole point of the split. docs/stack-notes.md gets its own header on line 1, '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2, notes tier. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.', and one marker pair holding the per-tool detail: role, how each tool is wired, the conventions it implies, and the Vite-7-needs-Node-20.19+ caveat. A third column of prose in docs/stack.md, or the whole reference written into one file, is the failure this pins. There is no previous section in either file, so nothing is carried and nothing is superseded, and the report says nothing needed carrying. The report states the byte size of each file's managed section and tail plus docs/stack.md's whole-file total, labelled as what loads at session start. Creates AGENTS.md with exactly the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md', path NOT in backticks, no HTML markers. NEITHER AGENTS.md NOR CLAUDE.md mentions docs/stack-notes.md at all: only docs/stack.md points at it, and only as a plain path. Creates CLAUDE.md containing the single line '@AGENTS.md' and no generated stack content. Creates the README with a Tech stack section + Getting started inside a <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> managed block with the 'generated/overwritten' note.

evals.name: infer-from-codebase
evals.prompt: There's no stack file for this project. Can you figure out what it's built with and document it? I want a reference my coding agents will pick up, and a tech stack + getting started in the README. If you need me to confirm what you inferred, treat this message as the confirmation and go ahead. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: No docs/stack.md, no docs/stack-notes.md, no lockfile, and no marker block in CLAUDE.md, so there is no format signal at all and nothing to migrate. The stack is inferred from the codebase (pyproject.toml + imports): Python >=3.12, FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0. The package manager is a guess: the [dependency-groups] table points at uv or another PEP 735 aware manager, and there is no uv.lock to settle it, so naming uv flatly is wrong. The Commands table still writes the commands in ONE form rather than hedging in the loaded tier, and uv is the reasonable read of [dependency-groups], so the rows are the uv forms (`uv sync`, `uv add <package>`, `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format .`, `uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload`); there is no build step in this project, so no build row. The guess is flagged BESIDE those commands in the notes tier, saying plainly that the manager was inferred from [dependency-groups] with no uv.lock to confirm it and that every command changes shape if the project turns out to use a different PEP 735 manager. A hedge inside docs/stack.md's Commands table, or an unflagged uv in the notes tier, are both failures. States plainly that the stack was inferred and what it was inferred from; does NOT fabricate a stack.yaml. docs/stack.md gets the format 2 header on line 1, one marker pair, the Commands table, a two-column Pins table, the Rules, and the plain-path pointer to docs/stack-notes.md as the last line inside the markers, no '@' anywhere near it. docs/stack-notes.md gets the notes-tier header on line 1 and the per-tool detail inside one marker pair. Neither file has a tail, nothing is carried, nothing is superseded. The report states the byte size of each file's managed section and tail plus docs/stack.md's whole-file total, labelled as what loads at session start. Creates AGENTS.md with the single pointer line, creates CLAUDE.md as the one-line '@AGENTS.md' bridge, and creates the README with its managed block.

evals.name: idempotent-refresh
evals.prompt: The stack changed. Please re-document it. The stack reference and the README section already exist; just bring them up to date. Then run it once more. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Both signals read 2, the docs/stack.md header and the lockfile's format key, so migrate must NOT run. The content is STALE in both tiers: docs/stack.md holds old facts (Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.110.0, 'Test: pytest', no uvicorn/Ruff), docs/stack-notes.md repeats them in its detail table, and the README's <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> block is stale too. Human-written prose lives in AGENTS.md (House rules, Deployment notes), outside the README markers (Contributing), below the end marker in docs/stack.md (a '## Local overrides' line about port 8100) and below the end marker in docs/stack-notes.md (a '## Team notes' section with two lines). Marker integrity runs on BOTH docs files AND the README before any of them is written. Re-running must (a) replace only what is between the markers in each docs file so both match the lockfile (FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0, Python 3.14.3), keeping each header line and leaving exactly one marker pair per file, (b) reproduce BOTH tails verbatim, same text and same blank lines: the '## Local overrides' line stays in docs/stack.md and the '## Team notes' section stays in docs/stack-notes.md, and neither moves to the other file, (c) refresh only what's between the README markers and preserve the prose outside them verbatim, with no second block appended, (d) leave AGENTS.md untouched, since it already contains @docs/stack.md, and leave the one-line '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md alone, (e) put no generated stack content into CLAUDE.md, (f) keep the two-column Pins table and the plain-path notes pointer in docs/stack.md, with the third column of detail in docs/stack-notes.md and nowhere else. Every line of the old sections is either a superseded version (Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.110.0), a command the new section restates in the project's own form ('pytest' becomes 'uv run pytest'), or a line the new render already states: SQLModel 0.0.22 matches the lockfile exactly, so it is SET ASIDE, not superseded, and it gets no report line. So NOTHING is carried: no '## Notes carried forward' heading and no provenance line appear in either file, and no scaffolding from the old sections ('# Stack', '## Commands', the table header rows) turns up below either end marker. The report lists the two superseded versions and the one superseded command on their own lines, since 'nothing needed carrying' is only said when that list is empty too. The report states the byte size of each file's managed section and tail plus docs/stack.md's whole-file total, labelled as what loads at session start. The second run produces the same two header lines, the same tools and versions, the same two tails, and no accumulated or duplicated content: its previous sections are ones this skill just wrote, so every line of them is already stated by the new render and nothing at all is carried, and this time nothing is superseded either. This is the skill's headline idempotency property.

evals.name: agents-md-has-human-rules
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack for the agents and for people, then do it again to check nothing drifts. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The lockfile is stamped format 2, AGENTS.md carries the pointer and CLAUDE.md is the '@AGENTS.md' bridge, but both docs files are missing: the pointer aims at a file that isn't there, which is a missing piece rather than an undocumented project. The skill must INVOKE stack-it:migrate, which writes both stubs (each with its header, one marker pair, and the single line 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.', and docs/stack.md also carrying the plain-path pointer sentence to docs/stack-notes.md) so the pointer resolves and the loaded file points at a notes file that exists, and the report must say migrate ran. document-stack then fills both sections from the lockfile: the stub line is a migrate marker, so it is dropped rather than carried, and NO stub text survives into either final file. Nothing else was in either section, so nothing is carried. AGENTS.md already holds human-written rules (function components only, co-located tests, second reviewer for src/api/, never commit .env) AND the pointer line. Across two consecutive runs: AGENTS.md ends with exactly ONE 'read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md' line and every human rule verbatim, in its original order, with the pointer still last and still unbackticked, and no line for docs/stack-notes.md is ever added to it. The presence check is on '@docs/stack.md', so the skill appends nothing even though it did not write that sentence itself. docs/stack.md carries its header, the Commands table with a row only for the scripts this project defines, a two-column Pins table (Vite 7.1.0, React 19.1.0, TypeScript 5.7.3, Tailwind 4.1.11, Vitest 3.2.0, ESLint 9.17.0), the Rules, and the plain-path notes pointer with no '@'; docs/stack-notes.md carries the wiring, including flat ESLint config from eslint.config.js and Tailwind v4 through the Vite plugin. On run two only the sections between the markers are rewritten: same header lines, same tools and versions, no accumulated content, no second marker pair in either file. migrate does not run again on the second pass. The report states the byte size of each file's managed section and tail plus docs/stack.md's whole-file total, labelled as what loads at session start. The one-line '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md is left alone both runs and never receives stack content. The README's managed block is created on run one and refreshed in place on run two, never duplicated.

evals.name: from-v1-layout
evals.prompt: Please re-document this project's stack. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Both readable signals say 1: .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml has no format key, and CLAUDE.md carries the marker block. There is no docs/stack.md, so the highest signal is 1. The skill must INVOKE stack-it:migrate rather than restructuring the layout itself, then continue once migrate reports 'migrated to 2'. migrate carries the old block into docs/stack-notes.md, under the line 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.' inside that file's markers, and writes docs/stack.md as a stub. End state: no <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> block anywhere in CLAUDE.md; CLAUDE.md starts with '@AGENTS.md' (the user said yes) followed by the House rules and Deployment notes prose intact; stack.yaml stamped 'format: 2' as its first key and still valid; docs/stack.md holding the format 2 header, the Commands table, a two-column Pins table and the Rules regenerated from the lockfile (FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0, Python 3.14.3), NOT the stale 0.110.0 text migrate carried in, and the plain-path notes pointer as its last line inside the markers; docs/stack-notes.md holding the per-tool detail regenerated from the same lockfile, with the carried placeholder line gone; AGENTS.md carrying the pointer line; the README block refreshed to the uv commands. Anything the carried block said that the new sections can't restate belongs below the end marker of docs/stack-notes.md under '## Notes carried forward', never in docs/stack.md's tail. This block says nothing of the sort: every line is a superseded version (Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.110.0), the command 'Test: pytest' which the new section restates as 'uv run pytest', or SQLModel 0.0.22, which matches the lockfile and is set aside. So nothing is carried and no '## Notes carried forward' heading appears in either file. The report lists each superseded version and command on its own line and states the byte size of each file's managed section and tail plus docs/stack.md's whole-file total, labelled as what loads at session start. Carrying the stale 0.110.0 line or the bare 'pytest' command into a tail is one failure this pins; dropping a note with no lockfile field behind it, letting a superseded version vanish without a report line, and putting carried text in docs/stack.md are the others. Exactly one layout at the end, never both. The report says migrate ran and what it moved.

evals.name: foreign-stack-doc
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md exists but was written by hand: its first line is '# Our stack, and why', which does not start with '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format', so the file is not ours. The ownership rule must STOP the run there and ask the user before touching the file, showing what's in it. It must NOT go on to use the other signals, which both read 1 (the lockfile has no format key, CLAUDE.md carries a marker block) and would start a migration. Nothing is written: docs/stack.md is not overwritten, no markers are inserted into it, no docs/stack-notes.md is created beside it, the CLAUDE.md block is still there with the House rules and Deployment notes around it, no AGENTS.md is created, no README is created. Nothing was written, so the report gives no file sizes; it gives the reason and the file. A cut CLAUDE.md block is the visible sign of the failure this pins, which is clobbering a human's hand-maintained stack document.

evals.name: format-ahead-of-plugin
evals.prompt: Bring the stack docs up to date for the project at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md and docs/stack-notes.md both carry valid generated headers reading 'format 3' while .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml says 'format: 2'. Reading every signal and taking the highest gives 3, which is ahead of the current format 2, so the skill stops and writes nothing and tells the user a newer stack-it wrote this project and the plugin should be upgraded. It must not downgrade either file, not overwrite either section inside its markers, and not settle on the lockfile's 2 because it looks current. migrate is not invoked. Nothing was written, so the report gives no file sizes; it gives the format it read and where it read it.

evals.name: recorded-decline-not-reasked
evals.prompt: Re-document the stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR, then run it once more.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md holds the user's own prose plus the pointer line, the recorded fallback from a run where they declined the '@AGENTS.md' import. AGENTS.md is the pointer-only file stack-it created. Across two runs the skill must NOT ask about the import again: the 'already contains @docs/stack.md outside backticks' case matches before the ask, so CLAUDE.md is left alone both times, with no '@AGENTS.md' line added and no second pointer line appended. Both docs files keep their headers and have only the sections between their markers refreshed from the lockfile. The old text across both sections is sorted line by line: 'Python 3.12' and 'FastAPI 0.110.0' are superseded versions and 'Test: pytest' is a command the new section restates as 'uv run pytest', so those three are dropped and reported; 'SQLModel 0.0.22' matches the lockfile, so it is set aside and not reported. NONE of the four may appear below either end marker. The '## Gotchas' line in docs/stack-notes.md about the lifespan handler creating the SQLite tables has no lockfile field behind it, so it is carried below THAT file's end marker under '## Notes carried forward' and listed in the report. Nothing is ever carried into docs/stack.md's tail, which stays empty. Nothing else is carried either: the '## Gotchas' heading above the note is scaffolding the new section restates in its own form, so the heading stays out of the tail and only the note itself moves. The heading is created with exactly one provenance line under it, 'Carried forward by stack-it. Each line says something the generated section above did not; prune what the section grows to cover.', undated so it is byte-stable. The report states the byte size of each file's managed section and tail plus docs/stack.md's whole-file total, labelled as what loads at session start. The second run must not duplicate that note or that line and must carry nothing new, and AGENTS.md and the README block are refreshed or left alone as usual.

evals.name: hand-tuned-block-survives
evals.prompt: Re-document this project's stack. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. Then run it once more. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: A format 1 project: the lockfile has no format key and CLAUDE.md carries the marker block, so migrate runs first. The block is not a plain render of the lockfile. Besides the tools list it holds three notes across four bullet lines that no lockfile field can express: the pnpm hoisting gotcha ('pnpm does not hoist. A package you import but never list in package.json resolves in local dev and fails at runtime on the build box; add it explicitly'), the Turbopack note ('serves stale CSS after renaming a module. Restart the dev server; a hard refresh does not clear it'), and the 'Built / pending' ledger (built: orders list, order detail, CSV export; pending: bulk refunds, audit log view, Stripe webhook replay). migrate must CARRY the whole block into docs/stack-notes.md under the placeholder line 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.' inside that file's markers, even though a valid lockfile exists: dropping it because the lockfile can regenerate the tools is the bug this eval exists for. It writes docs/stack.md as a stub at the same time, and both files land BEFORE it cuts the block, so a failure between the two leaves a duplicate rather than a hole. document-stack then regenerates both sections from the lockfile and the codebase only (Node.js 22.14.0, pnpm 10.4.1, Next.js 15.2.0, React 19.0.0, TypeScript 5.7.3, Tailwind CSS 4.0.9, Vitest 3.0.7, ESLint 9.21.0) and moves all three notes below the end marker of docs/stack-notes.md under a '## Notes carried forward' heading, with exactly one provenance line under the heading ('Carried forward by stack-it. Each line says something the generated section above did not; prune what the section grows to cover.'), and lists each note in the report so the user can prune it. docs/stack.md gets NONE of them: its tail stays empty and its managed section holds only the intro sentences, the Commands table, a two-column Pins table, the Rules, and the plain-path notes pointer. The report also names any carried note the new sections have grown to cover, as a prune candidate, and never edits either tail itself. The placeholder line is a migrate marker: dropped, never carried. The stale 'Next.js 15.1.0' pin does NOT survive anywhere, since it is a version the lockfile supersedes, and the report says so on its own line. The report states the byte size of each file's managed section and tail plus docs/stack.md's whole-file total, labelled as what loads at session start. End state: each docs file has its header on line 1 and exactly one marker pair; CLAUDE.md is '@AGENTS.md' followed by the rest of the file (title, House rules, Deployment notes) byte for byte; AGENTS.md carries the pointer; stack.yaml is stamped 'format: 2'. README.md has NO managed block to begin with, just a title, an intro line and a Contributing section, so run one INSERTS the block after the title and intro and above Contributing, and run two refreshes it in place: one pair, never a second block appended, and the Contributing prose verbatim both times. Nothing a human typed was lost. The second run replaces both sections again, leaves both tails alone, and carries nothing new: by then the previous sections are this skill's own output, so every line of them is already stated by the new render. No heading from either section ('# Stack', '## Commands', '# Stack notes') ever appears under '## Notes carried forward'; scaffolding is set aside, not carried. The second run reuses the existing heading and provenance line rather than writing a second of either.

evals.name: from-migrate-stub
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The lockfile has no format key and there is nothing else to read: no docs/stack.md, no docs/stack-notes.md, no CLAUDE.md, no AGENTS.md. A missing key reads as 1, so the project is behind and stack-it:migrate is invoked. migrate stamps 'format: 2', finds no block to move, and writes BOTH files as stubs: each gets its header, one marker pair, and the single line 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.', with docs/stack.md also carrying the plain-path pointer sentence to docs/stack-notes.md. It also creates the pointer and the '@AGENTS.md' bridge, then reports 'migrated to 2'. document-stack carries on and fills both sections from the lockfile (Python 3.14.3, uv 0.6.12, FastAPI 0.115.0, uvicorn 0.34.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0) with the real uv commands in docs/stack.md's Commands table and the per-tool detail in docs/stack-notes.md. The stub line is one of the two migrate markers, so it is dropped rather than carried: it must appear nowhere in either final file, above or below an end marker, and no '## Notes carried forward' heading is created, because there was nothing else in either section. The report says migrate ran, what it wrote, that nothing needed carrying, and states the byte size of each file's managed section and tail plus docs/stack.md's whole-file total, labelled as what loads at session start. The README gets its managed block.

evals.name: malformed-stack-doc
evals.prompt: Re-document the stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md is ours, its header prefix is right, and it holds a '<!-- stack-it:stack start -->' with NO matching end marker, so where the generated section stops is unknowable. docs/stack-notes.md beside it is well formed, which makes the broken file the only problem. Marker integrity runs on every present owned docs file BEFORE anything is judged missing, so the run stops here and writes NOTHING, anywhere: docs/stack.md is untouched, docs/stack-notes.md is untouched, no README is created, no AGENTS.md, no CLAUDE.md. It shows the user the offending lines and stops. Nothing was written, so the report gives no file sizes; it gives the offending lines. evals.name: oversized-block-splits-to-tiers
evals.prompt: Re-document this project's stack. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The structural-split case, and the reason format 2 has two tiers. What is under test here is WHERE each fact lands, not the 8 KB ceiling: this stack renders comfortably under it once the split is done, and no eval asserts a truncation. This is a format 1 project (the lockfile has no format key, CLAUDE.md carries the marker block), so migrate runs first and carries the block into docs/stack-notes.md. The block is 104 lines and about 8.3 KB: six pin tables whose third column is dense prose, a ten-row command table, six conventions, seven gotchas, and a built/pending ledger, covering roughly 29 tools. Rendered into one file the way format 1 did, that whole thing is charged to every session through the AGENTS.md pointer. document-stack must split it. docs/stack.md's managed section holds only the one or two opening sentences, the Commands table, a two-column Pins table under group headings, a Rules list of at most 15 lines, and the plain-path pointer to docs/stack-notes.md as its last line, with no '@' in front of it. docs/stack-notes.md's managed section takes the wiring and caveats the lockfile expresses: Tailwind v4 through the PostCSS plugin with tokens in app/globals.css and no tailwind.config.js, typedRoutes failing the build on a bad href, the Neon HTTP driver having no cross-statement transactions, the Stripe webhook needing the nodejs runtime, the Zod 3.x pin, the exact Auth.js beta pin, Playwright installing its own browsers, ESLint flat config, @vercel/og needing fonts as an ArrayBuffer, and the Sentry source-map upload needing SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN. CARRIED to docs/stack-notes.md's tail under '## Notes carried forward', because no lockfile field states them: six of the seven gotchas (the Turbopack stale-CSS restart, the Neon idle-branch wake-up, the e2e-against-dev flakiness, the migration lock on a shared Neon branch, the generic server-action error that is only readable in Sentry, and the Stripe warning about a body Next has already parsed, which is a different fact from the runtime caveat the lockfile carries); the built/pending ledger; and the pin-row sentences the render does not state. Each is carried as a WHOLE SENTENCE under a bullet naming its tool, never as a clause: TypeScript's 'Path alias `@/*` maps to the repo root, configured in `tsconfig.json` and mirrored in `vitest.config.ts`.', whose 'maps to the repo root' half the Rules already state, so that half is reported as a prune candidate; next-mdx-remote's 'Frontmatter is parsed by gray-matter and validated by the Zod schema in `lib/content.ts`; an unknown key is a build error on purpose.', whose validation half the lockfile notes already state, reported the same way; the class-variance-authority row about variants being declared there rather than in template strings; Zod's sentence about every route handler parsing input with a schema from `lib/schemas.ts`; husky's '--no-verify' sentence; the lint-staged row; Vitest's sentence about the config sharing the tsconfig path alias; and Vercel Analytics' 'Nothing else should import it.' Splitting inside any of these sentences to carry only its new clause is a failure: a mixed sentence goes whole and its stated part becomes a prune candidate.
